subject.title: Proposal: safer self-update with pre-update backup + health check + auto-rollback/restore

question: Should OpenClaw core own an integrated safe-update transaction with update-tied backups, health/smoke checks, and automatic package plus state rollback, or should this stay split across narrower updater, backup/restore, scanner, and external-updater work?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses core updater architecture, state backup/restore, secrets policy, downgrade compatibility, service management, and operator UX; automation cannot safely choose those product and security semantics from the current code alone.

options.title: Keep as core safe-update design
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical integrated workflow and use the narrower related items only as implementation slices.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical items
options.body: Close this only after maintainers create or select one canonical issue each for backup/restore, scanner, external updater, and rollback policy with this context linked there.

options.title: Defer to external updater boundary
options.body: Make the external-updater issue the owner for transaction semantics and limit core to the public APIs needed for backup, health, and restore hooks.

recommendation.title: Keep as core safe-update design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical integrated workflow and use the narrower related items only as implementation slices.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest maintainer-facing issue review already routed this to maintainer follow-up, and the decision is primarily product/security scope rather than a narrow code-owner repair.
